Istanbul Tourist Pass® Review: Is It Worth It?

Istanbul can fill your wish list before you even arrive. A morning exploring the courtyards of Topkapı Palace, a walk beneath the domes of Hagia Sophia, an evening watching the shoreline light up from the Bosphorus. The question is how to bring those experiences together, and still leave room for the city to surprise you.

Is Istanbul Tourist Pass® worth it?

The short answer

Istanbul Tourist Pass® can be worth it if your chosen experiences cost more separately than the pass, and you have time to enjoy them. Day Pass works particularly well for several visits over consecutive sightseeing days. Flexi Pass suits a personal shortlist spread over its five-day validity period. The right choice starts with what you want to experience.

Picture the Istanbul you came to see

Perhaps you want to see as much as possible during a short break. Perhaps you have a few must-see places in mind, with long lunches and neighbourhood walks in between. Istanbul Tourist Pass® gives you two ways to shape that trip: a Day Pass for fuller sightseeing days, or a Flexi Pass built around the experiences you choose.

Think of your first morning in the Old City. Hagia Sophia, the Blue Mosque and the Basilica Cistern are all part of the same historic neighbourhood, yet each opens a very different window onto Istanbul. A guided visit can help you connect those places with the stories behind them, turning a list of landmarks into a day that makes sense.

That is one of the useful things about Istanbul Tourist Pass®: the catalogue includes different ways to experience the city. Some visits come with a live guide; others pair entry with an audio guide so you can explore at your own pace. An evening cruise can give your trip an entirely different rhythm.

Choose how you like to explore

If you enjoy asking questions and hearing a place brought to life, look for a guided tour. If you prefer to linger over a courtyard or pause for photographs, an audio-guided visit may suit you better. Matching the visit format to your travel style makes the comparison more useful: you are choosing the experience you want to have, as well as the place you want to see.

  • Live guideGuided tourA guide leads the visit at a scheduled session. Live tours have their own language arrangements, so check the listing.
  • Your own paceAudio-guided entryEntry plus an audio guide on your phone, available in 25 languages. Download it before you go to listen offline.
  • Help at the doorHosted entryAssistance with meeting and entering. It does not mean a live guide accompanies you throughout the attraction.

Leave room for the moments between the landmarks

Your favourite memory of Istanbul may be a palace courtyard. It may also be the coffee you learned to make, a colourful street you wandered down or the view from the water after a busy day. The pass catalogue gives you ways to build that variety into your trip.

Choose the activities you genuinely want to do. A pass feels most useful when it helps you enjoy your own version of Istanbul, with enough space between visits to appreciate where you are.

Day Pass or Flexi Pass: which sounds like your trip?

The easiest way to choose is to imagine the pace of your days. Would you enjoy a morning landmark, another visit after lunch and an evening activity? Or would you rather book a few favourites and leave the rest of your time open?

Day Pass: for days you want to fill with discovery

Day Pass is a good starting point when several included experiences are already on your wish list. You choose a duration from one to seven consecutive calendar days, then plan your visits around the available opening times and sessions. Adding another included experience within that period does not mean buying another individual ticket.

For a first visit, that can be especially appealing: you can bring together major sights and a cruise, then see whether there is room for a workshop or another included activity. Choose enough days to enjoy the programme comfortably; the shortest pass is only the best value if its timetable works for you.

Flexi Pass: for the places you already know you want to see

Flexi Pass lets you build a selection of experiences and use them within five days from first use. It suits a trip with a clear shortlist: perhaps a palace, a guided landmark visit and an evening on the water, with unplanned time around them. Your price follows the selection you build.

That breathing room can be valuable if sightseeing is only part of your holiday. You can enjoy the experiences you have chosen while leaving time for shopping, café stops or exploring another neighbourhood.

Make the calculation personal

Write down your must-sees, compare the same visit formats and add up only what you expect to use. Then compare that total with Day Pass and Flexi. Any saving is more meaningful when it comes from experiences you already wanted, not extra stops added simply to make the numbers look better.

From choosing your pass to enjoying your first visit

Once you have a rough itinerary, the next step is getting the practical details in place. Istanbul Tourist Pass® is digital, with pass details, attraction QR codes and visit information in its app.

  1. Choose your optionSelect your Day Pass duration or build your Flexi selection. You start with a pass that matches your plans.
  2. Open your passFollow your purchase instructions to access your pass in the app. Your entry and visit details are close to hand.
  3. Arrange your visitsCheck which experiences need a reservation and book the required sessions. You can plan meals and travel around confirmed times.
  4. Check before setting outRead the meeting point, entry instructions and current opening information. You arrive knowing where to go and what to show.
  5. Enjoy the visitUse the QR code or meeting procedure specified for that experience. Each visit follows its own published entry process.

Keep the details together, then get on with your day

Having your visits organised in one app can make a busy sightseeing day feel easier to manage. You can look up the next meeting point, check reservation details and find the available audio content without searching through separate bookings. Download available audio guides before heading out if you would like to listen offline.

Audio guides are offered in 25 languages. Live guided tours have their own language arrangements, so check the individual listing when choosing a session. At eligible attractions, skip-the-ticket-line access lets you bypass the ticket-purchase queue; security checks still apply.

A local team when you need a hand

Questions often become very practical once you arrive: where exactly is the meeting point, or which instruction applies to your visit? The provider advertises 24/7 WhatsApp support, giving you a place to ask. Istanbul Tourist Pass® launched in 2014 and is sold by Cityberry Travel Agency, TÜRSAB member No. 11745. About the operator

The combination of entry details, visit guidance and access to support is part of what you are comparing alongside the price. For a first trip to a new city, that organisation can be an appealing part of the package.

Your Istanbul Tourist Pass® questions, answered

What is Istanbul Tourist Pass®?

Istanbul Tourist Pass® is a digital Istanbul city pass combining selected attraction visits and experiences. Day Pass gives access to its included catalogue for your chosen consecutive days; Flexi Pass covers the experiences in your purchased selection.

How much does Istanbul Tourist Pass® cost?

Day Pass costs €149 for 1 day, €189 for 2 days, €219 for 3 days, €239 for 4 days, €259 for 5 days, €279 for 6 days and €299 for 7 days per adult (checked 21 October 2026). A 1-day child pass for ages 5 to 12 is €139. Flexi Pass is priced by the experiences you select, at up to 40% below their separate prices.

Is Day Pass or Flexi Pass better for a first visit?

Day Pass is a useful starting point if you want several major sights and activities over consecutive days. Flexi is worth comparing if you have a smaller shortlist and prefer time between visits. Price the experiences you want and choose a pace you will enjoy.

How long is the pass valid?

Day Pass is available for 1 to 7 consecutive calendar days from first use, and each day ends at 23:59. Flexi Pass is valid for five days from first use. Check your chosen product's activation instructions before your first visit.

Does it include Hagia Sophia, Topkapı Palace and the Basilica Cistern?

The current Day Pass catalogue lists experiences at all three. Their formats differ: Hagia Sophia and Basilica Cistern are listed as guided visits, while Topkapı Palace is hosted entry with an audio guide. Check the individual listings for current coverage and reservations; Flexi requires you to select the experiences you want.

Will I still need to queue?

Eligible experiences offer skip-the-ticket-line access. Security checks remain, and scheduled tours require you to arrive for the stated meeting time. Read the entry instructions for each visit.

Do I need to book everything in advance?

Reservation requirements vary by experience. Check the app and individual listings after purchase, then reserve the visits that require a time slot. This is especially helpful when several activities need to fit into the same day.

Can I visit the same attraction twice?

No. The pass has a one-visit limit for each attraction. You can still visit several different attractions on the same day, within the pass's fair usage limit.

Is it the same as an Istanbul transport card or MuseumPass?

No. Istanbul Tourist Pass® is a sightseeing product. Ordinary public transport should be planned separately, and the official MuseumPass İstanbul has its own museum coverage and conditions. Compare each product with the services you actually want to use.

Who sells Istanbul Tourist Pass®?

Istanbul Tourist Pass® is sold by Cityberry Travel Agency, a TÜRSAB member travel agency (No. 11745). It launched in 2014 and is part of the istanbul.com brand family. Support is available on WhatsApp 24/7.

The bottom line

Choose the pass that fits the Istanbul you want to experience

If your wish list is full and you are looking forward to active sightseeing days, start with Day Pass. If you have a few favourites and want to take your time, build a Flexi selection. Compare your plans, check the practical details and choose the option that gives you the right balance of value and freedom.
